AchievementsRead.description: A person's practice record, computed from their whole marked history.
AchievementsRead.title: AchievementsRead

ActivityAccepted.description:
How many were new. A repeat is accepted and not recorded, which is a success
rather than an error.
ActivityAccepted.title: ActivityAccepted

ActivityBatch.description:
A batch, because the browser sends these as it goes and a tab closing
should not lose the last few.
ActivityBatch.title: ActivityBatch

ActivityIn.description:
One thing the browser saw somebody do.

`ref_id` is a string because the six kinds live in three slices and one is
not a row at all; resolving a ref into a screen is the frontend's job.
ActivityIn.title: ActivityIn

AppendTrainees.description:
Who has just arrived, and where they go.

`station_version_ids` pairs positionally with `trainee_ids` — the nth
arrival takes the nth station. Omit it and everyone joins the station the
circuit is currently running.
AppendTrainees.title: AppendTrainees

AttemptBriefRead.title: AttemptBriefRead

AttemptHistoryItem.description:
One row of "what have I sat", with its station named.

`has_result` rather than a status the client has to interpret: "is there
feedback to open" is the only question every screen listing these asks.
AttemptHistoryItem.title: AttemptHistoryItem

AttemptReviewRead.description: The management step: what the candidate should have covered.
AttemptReviewRead.title: AttemptReviewRead

AudienceIn.description:
How a client says who something is for.

Lives in core beside the rule, like `Page` and `CursorParams`, since all
three slices take the same three fields.
AudienceIn.title: AudienceIn

AudienceOut.description: Who something is for, as a reader sees it.
AudienceOut.title: AudienceOut

AuthResult.description: A finished sign-in. `status` distinguishes it from an MFA challenge on the same route.
AuthResult.title: AuthResult

file.description: A JPEG, PNG or WebP image
file.title: File

BulkCreateMemberships.description:
A team at once, in one request. Capped so one request cannot invite a whole
hospital by accident.
BulkCreateMemberships.title: BulkCreateMemberships

BulkCreateTrainees.description:
A spreadsheet's worth of trainees in one request.

The browser parses the file; the API takes rows. Capped so one request
cannot invite a whole university at once by accident.
BulkCreateTrainees.title: BulkCreateTrainees

BulkMembershipsResult.description: Who joined and who was already there, so a partial upload is not a mystery.
BulkMembershipsResult.title: BulkMembershipsResult

BulkRelease.description:
Several signed-off candidates to release at once.

Each carries its own evidence: a release re-checks it against what was
signed off, candidate by candidate.
BulkRelease.title: BulkRelease

BulkReleaseResult.description: Who was released and who was not, so a partial release is not a mystery.
BulkReleaseResult.title: BulkReleaseResult

BulkTraineesResult.description: Who was added and who was not, so a partial upload is not a mystery.
BulkTraineesResult.title: BulkTraineesResult

CandidateScenarioRead.description:
Candidate-facing keys that sit flat on the document rather than in a block.

Ortho's stations are shaped this way: an interview or a trauma list rather
than a consultation, so the brief is a scenario and a set of images.
CandidateScenarioRead.title: CandidateScenarioRead

Capabilities.description: What the caller may do, decided here rather than duplicated in the frontend.
Capabilities.title: Capabilities

CheckoutStarted.description: Where to send the customer. Nothing is granted until the webhook.
CheckoutStarted.title: CheckoutStarted

CircuitConsole.description: One request for the screen a supervisor runs an examination from.
CircuitConsole.title: CircuitConsole

CloseAccount.description: Confirm closing the account. A password when one is set, otherwise the word delete.
CloseAccount.title: CloseAccount

CloudCapacityRead.description:
How full LiveKit Cloud is, for the people watching it.

`active` is None when Redis cannot be asked, which is also what routes a
new session to our own workers — so None here is the thing to look at.
CloudCapacityRead.title: CloudCapacityRead

CloudSlotPost.description:
What the worker posts. `room_name` is fixed by `slot_payload_key` in its
own configuration, so the field name is part of the contract.
CloudSlotPost.title: CloudSlotPost

CohortCandidate.description: One candidate's standing in a sitting.
CohortCandidate.title: CohortCandidate

CohortSummary.description:
How a sitting's candidates compare, ranked.

Exam sittings only. A training circuit is people practising, and ranking
them against each other would turn practice into an assessment nobody
agreed to sit.
CohortSummary.title: CohortSummary

ConsoleStation.description: Null fields mean the version is not readable by this org, not that it is untitled.
ConsoleStation.title: ConsoleStation

CreateAttempt.description:
What a client may ask for directly.

Deliberately narrower than `attempts.create_attempt`. The other kinds are *about* something a
different feature owns — a slot, a set entry, a peer pairing, an earlier attempt. Taking those ids
straight from the body unverified once let a caller attach their attempt to another organisation's
exam slot or another person's set entry, so each of those kinds instead has its own route that
checks ownership: `POST /me/station-sets/{set_id}/entries/{entry_id}/attempts` for a set station
and its debrief, and the circuit itself for an exam slot (ADR 0018). `room_name` is likewise not
the client's to choose — `voice` derives it from the attempt.
CreateAttempt.title: CreateAttempt

CreateProgramme.description:
The exam this programme groups sittings under.

By code, resolved in the institution's own scope first: a school that has
written its own `plab` gets that one, not the platform's.
CreateProgramme.title: CreateProgramme

CreditSignup.description:
Ties the signed-in account to the visit that brought them.

Sent after registering, with the key the arrival was logged under; the
browser holds it and the backend never sees a partner cookie.
CreditSignup.title: CreditSignup

CvUploadResult.description:
What an upload answers with, before the model has read it.

The row exists and is `processing`; the structured sections arrive later, read back from the
list. The message sets the expectation that this is not instant.
CvUploadResult.title: CvUploadResult

Dashboard.description: A trainee's home screen: entitlements, progress, recent attempts and question sets.
Dashboard.title: Dashboard

DirectoryUser.description: One row of the account directory.
DirectoryUser.title: DirectoryUser

DoctorInformationRead.description: The candidate's brief: what the doctor has in front of them.
DoctorInformationRead.title: DoctorInformationRead

DomainComposition.description:
How many marked attempts landed red, amber or green on one domain.

83 and above is green, 50 to 83 is amber, below that is red.
DomainComposition.title: DomainComposition

DomainScore.description: One bar of the radar: a rubric domain, averaged across the attempts.
DomainScore.title: DomainScore

ExamDirectorySummary.description: How many accounts an exam has, split by paid/trial/not-started.
ExamDirectorySummary.title: ExamDirectorySummary

ExportedAttempt.description: One attempt this person ran, with its own transcript and marks.
ExportedAttempt.title: ExportedAttempt

ExportedProfile.description: The account fields the export carries about the person themselves.
ExportedProfile.title: ExportedProfile

ExportedResult.description: One mark the engine produced for an attempt.
ExportedResult.title: ExportedResult

ExportedTranscript.description: One attempt's delivery record and the turns it carries.
ExportedTranscript.title: ExportedTranscript

ExportedTranscriptMessage.description: One spoken turn, as the export hands it back.
ExportedTranscriptMessage.title: ExportedTranscriptMessage

ExtendEntitlement.description: Move the end date. `None` makes the grant open-ended.
ExtendEntitlement.title: ExtendEntitlement

FlagStationBody.description:
A report that one station is wrong.

Was served by `identity` with a docstring saying persistence is TODO, so the
button in the runner confirmed a report that went nowhere.
FlagStationBody.title: FlagStationBody

ortho_station_type.description: When exam_code is ortho: clinical, communication, prioritisation, or portfolio.
ortho_station_type.title: Ortho Station Type

GrantEntitlement.description:
An institution granting one of its people access to an exam it runs.

By email, as everything an administrator does is. `ends_at` left empty is
open-ended; an institution usually sets it to the end of the academic year.
GrantEntitlement.title: GrantEntitlement

InvitationRead.description:
A re-sent invitation. The token itself is never returned; it goes only to
the address it was minted for.

Shared by roster's and tenancy's resend routes.
InvitationRead.title: InvitationRead

JobRead.description: One queued job as procrastinate holds it.
JobRead.title: JobRead

JobsPage.description: Newest first, keyed on the job id; pass `next_before_id` back to continue.
JobsPage.title: JobsPage

LegacyExchangeRequest.description:
Trade a token one of the legacy backends issued for a platform pair.

`provider` is a closed set rather than a string because it selects the
secret the token is verified against; an open one would let the caller
choose its own key.
LegacyExchangeRequest.title: LegacyExchangeRequest

LibraryStationRead.description:
A platform library station as a browser sees it — the list, and a link
to one station by id.

Deliberately without `content`. The library is browsable by every signed-in
user, and the content is the patient brief, the examiner's context and the
marking guidance — reading it before sitting the station is reading the
answers. `version_id` is what a practice set or a circuit binds, so a
caller never needs the body to use one.
LibraryStationRead.title: LibraryStationRead

LiveBoard.description:
Everything running in one organisation, in one request.

`as_of` is the server time the numbers were computed against, so a client
can count down from the deadlines rather than waiting to be told again.
LiveBoard.title: LiveBoard

LiveCircuit.description: One examination in progress, as a row on the board.
LiveCircuit.title: LiveCircuit

LiveStation.description: The station a candidate is on now. Null when the circuit is on a break.
LiveStation.title: LiveStation

LogoutRequest.description:
The session to end.

Optional: without it every session ends, which is what "sign me out
everywhere" means. With it only the presented chain goes, so signing out on
a phone leaves the laptop signed in.
LogoutRequest.title: LogoutRequest

ManagementPlanRead.description: The model answer, readable once the consultation is over.
ManagementPlanRead.title: ManagementPlanRead

MeEventEnvelope.description:
One frame of the `/me/events` fan-in stream: a named event and its small id payload.

Every other stream's frame is the same shape as its `GET`'s response model, named by
`sse_responses`. `/me/events` multiplexes many differently-shaped events (`attempt`,
`practice.session_updated`, `cv.read`, `media.updated`, `coverage`, ...) onto one
connection, so there is no single response model to point at. This envelope documents
the shape every frame shares instead: the event's name, and a small object of the ids
naming what changed — never the changed data itself, which the client re-fetches.
MeEventEnvelope.title: MeEventEnvelope

MediaPage.description:
A page of the catalogue, and how many items matched the filters.

`total_count` counts everything matching the filters, not the reader's
entitlement: a locked item is still listed, with `locked: true`.
MediaPage.title: MediaPage

MediaSearchPage.description: A page of search hits, and how many the query matched.
MediaSearchPage.title: MediaSearchPage

MessageAccepted.description: Deliberately thin: an id, so support can be quoted one, and nothing else.
MessageAccepted.title: MessageAccepted

MfaCodeRequest.description: A current authenticator code, required to confirm, rotate or remove MFA.
MfaCodeRequest.title: MfaCodeRequest

MfaEnrolConfirmRequest.description: Confirm a pending authenticator during sign-in.
MfaEnrolConfirmRequest.title: MfaEnrolConfirmRequest

MfaEnrolStartRequest.description: The enrolment challenge from a sign-in that required a second factor.
MfaEnrolStartRequest.title: MfaEnrolStartRequest

MfaEnrolmentConfirmed.description: A sign-in that has just confirmed an authenticator, plus the codes shown once.
MfaEnrolmentConfirmed.title: MfaEnrolmentConfirmed

MfaEnrolmentRequiredResponse.description: A second factor is required and this account has not confirmed one yet.
MfaEnrolmentRequiredResponse.title: MfaEnrolmentRequiredResponse

MfaEnrolmentStart.description: The shared secret and the URI an authenticator app scans. Shown once.
MfaEnrolmentStart.title: MfaEnrolmentStart

MfaRecoveryCodesRead.description: Recovery codes in plaintext. The only response that ever contains them.
MfaRecoveryCodesRead.title: MfaRecoveryCodesRead

MfaRequiredResponse.description: The password was right and an authenticator is already confirmed.
MfaRequiredResponse.title: MfaRequiredResponse

MfaStatusRead.description: Whether this account has an authenticator, and whether policy requires one.
MfaStatusRead.title: MfaStatusRead

MfaVerifyRequest.description: Redeem a sign-in challenge with an authenticator code or a recovery code.
MfaVerifyRequest.title: MfaVerifyRequest

MyDataExport.description: Everything `GET /me/export` hands back: one person's own data.
MyDataExport.title: MyDataExport

MySittings.description: The trainee portal's whole screen, in one request: what they are rostered onto.
MySittings.title: MySittings

MySlot.description: A station this person is rostered onto, from their side of it.
MySlot.title: MySlot

MySlotReviewRead.description:
A candidate's own read of their slot's review: the RAG summary and the
GP-lead's written feedback, once one has been completed. Never a
reviewer's draft, and never who observed them.
MySlotReviewRead.title: MySlotReviewRead

OnboardingScene.description: One demo scenario. The spelling is the worker's and the browser's.
OnboardingScene.title: OnboardingScene

OrgAtRisk.description: An organisation the console should look at before it looks at anything else.
OrgAtRisk.title: OrgAtRisk

OrgSetup.description:
Whether the organisation can actually hold a sitting yet.

Each flag is a step the browser was deriving from a list it fetched only to
take the length of.
OrgSetup.title: OrgSetup

Override.description:
Why the override was done. Optional free text, recorded beside the
action for later review.
Override.title: Override

PatientIdentityRead.description: Who the candidate is about to speak to, for the consultation header.
PatientIdentityRead.title: PatientIdentityRead

PatientReviewRead.description:
The patient's side, as a candidate may read it afterwards.

Not a passthrough: `persona`, `opening_sentence`, `expanded_history` and the hidden question list
are how the patient is played, and stay on the server. What is here is the biodata line and the
ideas, concerns and expectations the candidate was supposed to draw out.
PatientReviewRead.title: PatientReviewRead

PayoutDetailsAdminRead.description:
A referrer's bank details, decrypted, as platform admin settlement needs them.

Never returned to anyone but the person settling the payout — the account
number is in full here, unlike `PayoutDetailsRead`.
PayoutDetailsAdminRead.title: PayoutDetailsAdminRead

PayoutDetailsRead.description:
A referrer's own bank details, as they see them on reload.

The sort code only identifies a branch, not an account, so it is shown in
full — matching how the retiring client redisplayed it. The account
number stays masked to its last four digits.
PayoutDetailsRead.title: PayoutDetailsRead

PayoutDetailsWrite.description:
What a referrer submits to save or update their bank details.

`account_number` is optional so someone can change their bank name
without retyping a number that never left the client the first time
around; the service keeps the previously stored number when this is
omitted, and refuses with `payout_account_number_required` if none was
ever stored.
PayoutDetailsWrite.title: PayoutDetailsWrite

Performance.description:
The performance charts for one exam. `exam_code` is null only when the caller named
no exam and has never attempted one.
Performance.title: Performance

PerformanceSummary.description: How the marked attempts divide, as rates rather than counts.
PerformanceSummary.title: PerformanceSummary

PlatformAttemptRead.description:
An attempt, with the state a support question turns on.

`scoring_job` is the newest marking job for it, or None when nothing was
ever queued — which with a complete transcript is itself the diagnosis.
PlatformAttemptRead.title: PlatformAttemptRead

PlatformAuditRead.description:
An audit row as the console reads it across every organisation. `org_id` is None for
the platform's own acts.
PlatformAuditRead.title: PlatformAuditRead

PlatformEntitlementRead.description: A grant as the platform console reads it: where it came from, who made it.
PlatformEntitlementRead.title: PlatformEntitlementRead

A platform admin granting access outright — a refund made good, a
sponsor's seat, a support gesture. `note` is why, and goes in the audit row.
PlatformGrantEntitlement.title: PlatformGrantEntitlement

PlatformHealth.description: The liveness report plus what only the console needs: the queue and the worker.
PlatformHealth.title: PlatformHealth

PlatformPaymentRead.description: A payment as the console reads it: raw amounts, both references, what it bought.
PlatformPaymentRead.title: PlatformPaymentRead

PlatformUserDetail.description: Support view: memberships and account flags the list row omits.
PlatformUserDetail.title: PlatformUserDetail

PrioritisationPatientRead.description: One patient on an Ortho prioritisation list.
PrioritisationPatientRead.title: PrioritisationPatientRead

QueueStatus.description:
Where someone stands, and what to do next.

`position` is why this is one call: a polling client should be able to
answer "am I matched yet?" in one round trip.
QueueStatus.title: QueueStatus

ReadoutSitting.description: The sitting, as the head of the document states it.
ReadoutSitting.title: ReadoutSitting

ReadoutSummary.description: What the cohort adds up to. Counts, not judgements.
ReadoutSummary.title: ReadoutSummary

RebuildCircuit.description:
A circuit's full new roster and stations.

Both lists are sent whole, not as a patch: the slots are rebuilt from
them. `name`, `supervisor_user_id` and `timing` are left as they are when
omitted.
RebuildCircuit.title: RebuildCircuit

ReceiptRead.description:
A payment receipt, rendered. Every field is a string already formatted for display, so
two clients cannot render the same payment differently.
ReceiptRead.title: ReceiptRead

RecordArrival.description: Public: a visitor landing from a partner link, before any account exists.
RecordArrival.title: RecordArrival

RecordManualPayment.description:
A payment that did not come through Stripe — a bank transfer, a sponsor,
a comped seat — recorded so it grants access, mints a receipt and counts
like any other. Without a reference one is minted as `manual:<id>`.
RecordManualPayment.title: RecordManualPayment

ReferralAdminRead.description:
One referral, as the person settling it needs to see it.

Emails rather than ids: a uuid is not on a bank statement.
ReferralAdminRead.title: ReferralAdminRead

ReferralHistoryRead.description:
One redeemed referral, as the person who issued the code reads their own history.

`referee_email` is exposed here (unlike `ReferralAdminRead`'s two-sided
view being admin-only): this row belongs to the caller, and the retiring
client's history table names the referee in its "Referee Email" column.
ReferralHistoryRead.title: ReferralHistoryRead

RefundRequest.description:
Record-only: the money is returned in the Stripe dashboard. This revokes
what the payment bought and says so in the audit log; the payment row stays.
RefundRequest.title: RefundRequest

ReindexReport.description: What a re-index did, so an admin can tell "ran" from "found nothing".
ReindexReport.title: ReindexReport

RenewContract.description: New contract dates, and whether a suspension should lift with them.
RenewContract.title: RenewContract

RescoreRequest.description:
Re-queue the marking. Left empty, under the policy the attempt was
frozen with; named, under another one, whose result sits beside the old.
RescoreRequest.title: RescoreRequest

ResolveRosterRequest.description: Who a circuit would name, before it is built.
ResolveRosterRequest.title: ResolveRosterRequest

ResolvedRoster.description:
Who a circuit would actually contain, and what is missing.

Returned before a circuit is built so a supervisor sees an empty linked
group now rather than when the examination starts.
ResolvedRoster.title: ResolvedRoster

ResultAcknowledgement.description: A candidate's confirmation that they have read their result.
ResultAcknowledgement.title: ResultAcknowledgement

SaveDecision.description:
A decision to save as a draft.

`expected_revision` is the revision this screen last read, or 0 when it has
read nothing. A save that does not name the current one is refused with
`decision_revised` (409), so two administrators cannot overwrite each
other's draft.
SaveDecision.title: SaveDecision

SaveGpLeadReview.description:
`revision` is what the client last read.

Required, so a client that does not send it cannot overwrite blindly.
SaveGpLeadReview.title: SaveGpLeadReview

ScoringJobRead.description: One marking job as the queue holds it.
ScoringJobRead.title: ScoringJobRead

SearchHit.description: One search match. `excerpt` defaults to empty; this backend always fills it in.
SearchHit.title: SearchHit

SessionFeedback.description:
What one participant leaves after a session, matching what the legacy form asked for.

`would_practice_again` is the one field the legacy form always required —
a session either felt worth repeating or it did not, and that answer is
what a good-match signal is built from. The star rating was always
optional there, which this keeps: someone declining to rate a partner is
not the same as having nothing to say about practising with them again.
SessionFeedback.title: SessionFeedback

SetPlatformAdmin.description: Grant or revoke, spelled out rather than implied by which route was called.
SetPlatformAdmin.title: SetPlatformAdmin

SiteStatistics.description:
The counters the landing page's numbers band shows.

Marketing figures, not analytics: they are rounded down to a readable
number and they are cached, because the busiest page on the site should not
cost five aggregate queries per view.
SiteStatistics.title: SiteStatistics

SittingReadout.description: Everything the read-out says, in the order it says it.
SittingReadout.title: SittingReadout

SlotRagSummary.description:
What several reviewers of one slot agreed, or did not.

The worst rating wins per domain: when reviewers disagree, the lower
rating is the one that should prompt a conversation.
SlotRagSummary.title: SlotRagSummary

SsoCallbackRequest.description:
The token the broker handed back, and the organisation it was for.

`state` (SEC-015) is the signed anti-forgery value the sign-in URL carried
and the OIDC provider echoed back on the redirect. It is optional on the
contract — Clerk's flow does not carry one — but required for a provider
that runs the code flow (Entra), which the callback enforces.
SsoCallbackRequest.title: SsoCallbackRequest

SsoConfigRead.description: The whole arrangement, for whoever administers it.
SsoConfigRead.title: SsoConfigRead

SsoLoginRequest.description:
Which organisation to start signing in to.

The slug comes from `GET /auth/sso/sign-in`, which a sign-in page already
called to learn whether this visitor's organisation signs in elsewhere.
SsoLoginRequest.title: SsoLoginRequest

SsoLoginResult.description:
Where to send the browser to sign in.

A URL rather than a server-side redirect: the frontend owns navigation
and the platform issues no cookies (ADR 0004).
SsoLoginResult.title: SsoLoginResult

SsoSession.description:
A platform session — what a login returns, minus the profile.

The frontend stores these and reads the person from `GET /me`, so the user
object is not duplicated into this slice's contract; `identity` owns its
shape and the broker's job ends at the tokens.
SsoSession.title: SsoSession

SsoSignIn.description:
What a sign-in page may show before anybody has proved anything.

Deliberately thin: served without a token, to anyone who asks. No
issuer, no bindings, no counts — those are configuration.
SsoSignIn.title: SsoSignIn

StaffMfaPolicy.description: Whether this organisation's staff must sign in with a second factor.
StaffMfaPolicy.title: StaffMfaPolicy

StartCheckout.description: Which plan to buy. A code, never a price: the plan row owns the price.
StartCheckout.title: StartCheckout

StartedAttempt.description:
What starting a set entry returns.

Deliberately this slice's own shape rather than `attempts`' response model.
They would look alike today and diverge the moment either contract moves,
and a client of one should not break because the other added a field.
StartedAttempt.title: StartedAttempt

StationPhotosResult.description:
The version as it now stands, and anything that did not make it.

A partial upload is a result rather than an error: the files that worked
are on the station, and the caller is told which ones were not.
StationPhotosResult.title: StationPhotosResult

StationProgressChange.description: What one of the two actions did, in numbers the toast can print.
StationProgressChange.title: StationProgressChange

StationProgressRead.description:
One station this person has sat, or holds in a practice set.

`attempts` counts the attempts that exist; `entry_attempts` is the sum of
the counters on their set entries, which is what the per-station limit is
enforced on and what "reset attempts" zeroes. The two agree until somebody
resets, and showing both is how the console explains the difference.
StationProgressRead.title: StationProgressRead

StationTeachingRead.description: Ortho's flat teaching keys: the debrief material for a non-consultation station.
StationTeachingRead.title: StationTeachingRead

StreamTicket.description:
A short-lived credential for one `EventSource` connection.

`EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header; see `core.streams` for
why this exists rather than a cookie or a token in the query string.
StreamTicket.title: StreamTicket

StripeEventRead.description:
One webhook delivery from the ledger, with the fields support reads
out of the payload rather than the whole document.
StripeEventRead.title: StripeEventRead

StructuredCv.description: The sections a CV is read into. A section with nothing in it is null.
StructuredCv.title: StructuredCv

SupervisorCircuitRow.description: One circuit this person is named on, with the sitting it belongs to.
SupervisorCircuitRow.title: SupervisorCircuitRow

SwitchWorkspace.description:
Which workspace to re-issue the token against. `None` means the person's own practice
— a real destination, not an absence.
SwitchWorkspace.title: SwitchWorkspace

ToolCall.description:
What the worker posts for one tool call.

`call_id` is the worker's own and is echoed nowhere; it is here because the
worker sends it and a rejected extra field would fail the call.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolResult.description:
What the model reads, and what the browser is shown.

`result` is spoken, so it is prose rather than data. `display` is passed to
the frontend unchanged on the data channel; the backend never composes a
route, because which screen a thing lives on is the frontend's business.
ToolResult.title: ToolResult

TrackingReference.description: What a partner puts in one link, and where that link points.
TrackingReference.title: TrackingReference

TraineeResultRead.description:
A candidate's own view of their result.

Deliberately narrower than the internal record: moderation notes and the
evidence snapshot stay internal.
TraineeResultRead.title: TraineeResultRead

TrendPoint.description: One attempt, in the order it was sat.
TrendPoint.title: TrendPoint

TutorMemoryRead.description:
Everything the tutor holds about you, in the order it would speak it.

Exists so "what do you know about me" is answerable without reading a
prompt: a memory nobody can inspect is one nobody can correct.
TutorMemoryRead.title: TutorMemoryRead

UpdateBrief.description: The one field a published version will accept a change to.
UpdateBrief.title: UpdateBrief

UpdateCohort.description:
Rename an intake, or say which academic year it belongs to. Fields left out
are unchanged.
UpdateCohort.title: UpdateCohort

UpdateExam.description: Everything but the code, which existing plans and ref ids depend on.
UpdateExam.title: UpdateExam

UpdateGroup.description: Rename a group. Membership does not change.
UpdateGroup.title: UpdateGroup

UpdateMe.description: What a person may change about themselves. Absent means "leave it".
UpdateMe.title: UpdateMe

UpdateOrganization.description: What a platform administrator may change about an organisation. Not the slug.
UpdateOrganization.title: UpdateOrganization

UpdateSet.description:
What a learner may still change about a set they have built.

The name, and — since this replaces the legacy "edit session" screen — the
stations themselves. Swapping the list does not touch an entry that stays
in it: its counters are what an attempt points at, so `replace_entries`
matches kept versions back onto their existing entry rather than deleting
and recreating it. A set carries no description and no timings — the
length of a session is the sum of its stations' exam timings, which the
exam owns — so there is nothing else to write.

Whitespace strips to nothing, which is then too short: a set called `"   "`
is an unlabelled row in the list the learner has to keep.

`station_version_ids` left out (`None`) means "just the name"; an empty
list is a real request to empty the set, and is rejected only if that
would mean removing a station that already has an attempt against it.
UpdateSet.title: UpdateSet

UpdateSitting.description:
Fields to change on a sitting. An omitted field is left alone.

`status` is not offered here: that belongs to the run machine, not this
route.
UpdateSitting.title: UpdateSitting

UpdateStationFlag.description:

slice landed, and nothing called it — the b2c debrief had no way in.
